comment: Known disagreements scripts/formal/refdiff-harness.py --ci accepts. Each rule names the harness classes it covers; `pointer` (exact), `pointer_suffix` and `verdict`, when present, must match the record (`verdict`: both records'); `requires: alias-loop` is checked by the harness (q1_checker): the record's use must reach, on either side, a component in an alias loop or leading into one that is named by the record's ref: values or its counterpart's at the same use, owner and pointer, or by its owner pair when that component is a pure alias ({$ref} and nothing else after canonicalisation). formal/refdiff/negative/ holds corruptions this must reject. See formal/README.md, "Reference semantics of `$ref` diffs", Known limits.

rules.name: Q1: content-free alias loop (C = {"$ref": C}, or a ref cycle with no content) facing an undeclared ref or inline schema: the model takes the fixpoint, the Rust compares the literal $ref; one Review record at a $ref key either way
#186: the Rust follows component references outside the schema grammar (default, if, prefixItems, $defs, ...) and rates what it finds there by the direction table; the model does not follow them
